text:
Sam Li: quick q — thinking about whether we should push a tiny delegated "warmup" contract API to the operator vs building a single centralized prewarm service for all pools. tradeoffs? :thinking:
Priya Nair: delegate sounds nice for operator minimalism. each pool owns its own warmup lifecycle so less central state.
Ben Ortiz: but more surface area — every operator needs to implement lease + warmup semantics. that could lead to divergence.
Sam Li: right. current idea: a small idempotent RPC `ReserveWarm(pool_id, model, slots, ttl)` that returns a `warm_handle` and success/failure. operator decides how to satisfy it (prestart, keepalive, queue).
Mei Chen: can you paste the proto?
Sam Li: sure:
```
service WarmService {
  rpc ReserveWarm(ReserveRequest) returns (ReserveReply);
}
message ReserveRequest { string pool_id = 1; string model = 2; int32 slots = 3; int32 ttl_s = 4; }
message ReserveReply { bool ok = 1; string warm_handle = 2; string reason = 3; }
```
Priya Nair: I like the simplicity. operator-local decisions -> improved failure isolation. If central service is down, only pools using it are impacted, not the whole control plane.
Ben Ortiz: counterpoint: observability + billing. central service can aggregate metrics and enforce global quotas (eg total prewarm GPU-budget). with delegated, we need cross-operator accounting.
Mei Chen: we could emit standardized metrics from operators (warm.reserve_attempts, warm.failures, warm.active_handles) and have a collector job to aggregate. avoids tight coupling.
Sam Li: also worried about races: two controllers reserve same slot for different tenants if delegation is local. we need a consistent admission path for physical device allocation.
Priya Nair: admission should still go through the allocator. ReserveWarm is advisory: operator asks allocator for N prewarm slots with a special policy flag. allocator remains the single source of truth for device assignment.
Ben Ortiz: that works. the allocator becomes the choke point for global capacity — good. but then operators must translate warm_handle -> allocator lease id. complexity shifts but stays centralized where it matters.
prewarm-bot: NOTE: warm_handles should have TTL enforcement. stale handles will be reclaimed after ttl + grace.
Mei Chen: rollout plan thought: start with delegated ReserveWarm implemented in one operator shard, emit metrics, then pilot the collector to validate global budget behavior. no central API at first.
Sam Li: agree. next questions: billing + cost attribution. ReserveWarm should include "purpose" or tenant metadata so meter can charge warm minutes separately.
Ben Ortiz: add a small auth token in the API so operator can validate caller identity. also return a best-effort estimate of expected cost per minute in reply.
Priya Nair: and a fallback: if ReserveWarm fails, caller can optionally request a cold-start route with lower latency SLA. important for user-facing spikes.
Sam Li: sweet. will sketch RFC with proto + allocator integration notes. plan: prototype on staging operator 42, collect metrics for 2 weeks, then decide whether to add a centralized coordinator for budget enforcement if collector approach shows gaps.
Mei Chen: please add a short section in RFC about monitoring hooks and the required labels for logs/metrics. makes the collector job doable.
Sam Li: will do. thanks all :thumbsup:
